subject.title: [Bug]:  [Windows] exec spawn: all commands hang with no output (stdio pipe deadlock)

question: Does a maintainer have native Windows proof that current main fixes the reported all-command no-output exec hang, or should this stay open for reproduction?
rationale: Source inspection shows relevant hardening but cannot prove the native Windows PowerShell-started gateway path without a real Windows run.

options.title: Keep pending native proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a native Windows run captures `echo hello` and `node -v` behavior on current main and identifies the failing process path if it still hangs.

options.title: Close with proof
options.body: Close as implemented only if maintainers can attach current-main or shipped-release native Windows proof showing the exact reported commands complete with output.

recommendation.title: Keep pending native proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a native Windows run captures `echo hello` and `node -v` behavior on current main and identifies the failing process path if it still hangs.
